<h2 id="D2-%E2%80%94-Model-comparison-(same-split,-same-features)">D2 — Model comparison (same split, same features)<a class="anchor-link" href="#D2-%E2%80%94-Model-comparison-(same-split,-same-features)">¶</a></h2>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noInput" id="cell-id=d12">
<div class="jp-Cell-outputWrapper">
<div class="jp-Collapser jp-OutputCollapser jp-Cell-outputCollapser">
</div>
<div class="jp-OutputArea jp-Cell-outputArea">
<div class="jp-OutputArea-child">
<div class="jp-RenderedText jp-OutputArea-output" data-mime-type="text/plain" tabindex="0">
<pre>                                                                  rmse     mae  train_s
model                                                                                  
LightGBM (default params)                                        9.006   5.981   16.448
Baseline: seasonal naive (zone × weekday × hour, last 8 weeks)   9.558   6.405    0.018
Random forest                                                    9.757   6.468   10.122
Ridge regression                                                10.341   7.006    1.135
Baseline: mean predictor                                        27.504  20.677    0.001

Winner: LightGBM (default params) — lowest RMSE and MAE on the main fortnight. Gradient boosting fits the interactions between zone, hour, weekday, recent demand, rain and events without hand-made interaction terms, and the Poisson objective suits count data. Ridge needs interactions spelled out; the random forest is slower and averages away sharp peaks.
</pre>

<h2 id="D8-%E2%80%94-Response-to-findings">D8 — Response to findings<a class="anchor-link" href="#D8-%E2%80%94-Response-to-findings">¶</a></h2>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=d29">
<div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0">
<div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser">
</div>
<div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown">
<p>Change tried because of D7: <strong>weight recent weeks more</strong> when training (demand grew ~41% Jan→Oct, so the model under-predicts the latest fortnights — positive bias in D7). Sample weight = 0.5 for the oldest rows rising linearly to 1.5 for the newest. Same folds, same features, same parameters.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noInput" id="cell-id=d30">

model                                                           
LightGBM (tuned)                        9.394    0.864     6.066
LightGBM (tuned) + recency weights      9.539    0.953     6.132
bias by fold after the change: {1: 0.72, 2: 0.89, 3: 0.43, 4: 0.51}

Result: it did not help — kept the previous final model.
</pre>

<h2 id="D9-%E2%80%94-Plain-language-metric">D9 — Plain-language metric<a class="anchor-link" href="#D9-%E2%80%94-Plain-language-metric">¶</a></h2>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noInput" id="cell-id=d32">
<div class="jp-Cell-outputWrapper">
<div class="jp-Collapser jp-OutputCollapser jp-Cell-outputCollapser">
</div>
<div class="jp-OutputArea jp-Cell-outputArea">
<div class="jp-OutputArea-child">
<div class="jp-RenderedText jp-OutputArea-output" data-mime-type="text/plain" tabindex="0">
<pre>Trips per active driver per hour in the history: 1.27

On the last validation fortnight (18–31 Oct) a typical zone-hour has 33 trips. Our forecast is off by about 6.0 trips on an average zone-hour (MAE, 18% of demand); the RMSE of 8.9 trips (27%) is larger because it weighs the occasional big miss more. At about 1.3 trips per driver per hour, that is roughly 5 drivers too many or too few in a typical zone-hour, and around 7 drivers in the busier, harder hours.
</pre>

<h2 id="Final-model-%E2%86%92-test-predictions-(1%E2%80%9314-Nov-2025)">Final model → test predictions (1–14 Nov 2025)<a class="anchor-link" href="#Final-model-%E2%86%92-test-predictions-(1%E2%80%9314-Nov-2025)">¶</a></h2>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=d40">
<div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0">
<div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser">
</div>
<div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown">
<p>The final model is re-trained on <strong>all</strong> cleaned train rows (1 Jan – 31 Oct 2025) with the chosen settings, then predicts every test row. Test features come from <code>master_test.csv</code>, built by the same pipeline as train; lags use only train history and November weather is the forecast in the weather file. <code>predicted_trips</code> is rounded to whole trips (the model predicts an expected count; rounding changed validation RMSE by less than 0.01). The submission keeps the test file's original row order.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noInput" id="cell-id=d41">
<div class="jp-Cell-outputWrapper">
<div class="jp-Collapser jp-OutputCollapser jp-Cell-outputCollapser">
</div>

<div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown">
<p><code>models/final_model.joblib</code> holds the trained model plus everything needed to build its inputs (feature order, zone codes, zone types), its settings, validation scores and library versions; <code>final_model_lightgbm.txt</code> is the same model in LightGBM's own format as a version-proof fallback. The demo app reads only <code>app/assets/</code>: the model, the November feature rows, the cleaned events and weather, each zone's average fare and typical profile from the history, and the validation results.</p>
